page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Apocarpous
lines: Apocarpous: the gynoecium has more than one
carpel and the carpels are FREE from one
steps.why: Apo = apart: each carpel stands free on the thalamus. Both conditions need more than one carpel - free versus fused is the only difference.
common_mistakes: Applying the terms to a single-carpel flower. With one carpel the question of free or fused does not arise.
steps.memory_tip: Apo - apart; carpels kept separate, as in lotus.
steps.margin_note: Definition + one example; a two-column table also works.

steps.label: Syncarpous

lines.text: Syncarpous: the carpels are FUSED with one

steps.why: Syn = together: the carpels are joined into one ovary, as in mustard (two fused carpels).
common_mistakes: Swapping the examples - lotus is apocarpous; mustard and tomato are syncarpous.
steps.memory_tip: Syn - together, like synthesis: carpels joined.
steps.margin_note: FREE vs FUSED is the tested pair - make both words visible.
